title: Import handoff manifest
description: handoff.json, the share extension's commit record in the App Group inbox (plan 6.1, 8.1; ADR-0010). The extension streams every item into <inbox>/<handoff_id>/items/, syncs it, and writes this file last, atomically (temporary file, F_FULLFSYNC, rename without replace, directory sync). It reports receipt only after that. A handoff directory without this file is incomplete by definition and is never imported. Rules the schema cannot express and readers must enforce: handoff_id equals the name of the directory holding the file; stored_path values and item_id values are unique; total_bytes is the sum of byte_count; the items directory holds exactly the listed files, each a regular file whose size and SHA-256 match. original_filename is metadata only and is never used as a path. Readers also refuse, beyond what this schema checks (ADR-0010; G0.3 report F16): a text that is not strict JSON (RFC 8259) in UTF-8 without a byte order mark; a member name given twice in one object; an unpaired surrogate escape; nesting deeper than 512 levels; an integer of more than 4300 digits; NaN or Infinity; integers outside the readers' 64-bit fields (byte_count and total_bytes above 18446744073709551615); a UUID not in the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form of RFC 4122; and a date-time or pattern-checked string that ends in a line feed, which RFC 3339 and ECMA-262 refuse although Python's re lets $ match before a final line feed. Readers also refuse a handoff.json of more than 256 KiB (262144 bytes), whitespace and unknown members included, and writers must not produce one: Sylvia's share extension refuses to commit one and shows its fallback instead. 100 items with 255-byte file names and 128-character type identifiers take 87803 bytes (G0.3 review R4-02). The file is private to the app and its extension, never leaves the device, and holds no credential.

handoff_id.description: UUID generated by the extension; also the handoff directory's name.

total_bytes.description: Sum of every item's byte_count, in bytes.

stored_path.description: Relative to the handoff directory: items/<ordinal> with an optional lowercase alphanumeric extension. Generated by the extension, never derived from the shared file name beyond its sanitized extension.

original_filename.description: The shared file's name, for display only. At most 255 UTF-8 bytes. maxLength here counts code points, so for non-ASCII text it admits names over the byte limit, which writers must not produce and readers refuse. Example: 'é' 128 times is 128 code points and 256 bytes: valid against this schema, refused by readers. The pattern excludes the code points '/' and U+0000 anywhere, including a '/' followed by a combining mark, which a grapheme-cluster comparison such as Swift's String.contains does not see (G0.3 report F18).

content_type.description: Uniform type identifier of the supported type the item was received as (EPUB, PDF, plain text, Markdown or audio).

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes, computed while streaming the copy.

representation.description: file_representation: an NSItemProvider file representation of a supported type. file_url: a public.file-url item the extension could read.

provider_type_identifier.description: The type identifier the item was loaded with.
